role: General secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (2012–present); president of China (2013–present)
summary: Xi advocates Communist Party leadership, socialist modernisation and national reunification. He supports a mixed economy under party leadership, technological development, cultural continuity and a larger developing-country voice in international governance.

accelerate-technology.rationale: In "Transition to Innovation-driven Growth" he urges China to catch up and surpass in a new technological revolution and move faster to innovation-driven growth; he does not discuss disrupting existing institutions.

ban-cartels.rationale: The 20th Congress report commits to stronger action against monopolies and unfair competition and to breaking administrative monopolies and local protectionism; the 2013 Decision explained in the Third Plenum notes also aims at a unified, fairly competitive market.

central-planning.rationale: He replaced the "basic" market role with a "decisive" market role ("The Invisible Hand and the Visible Hand", Economic Development) and urges government to withdraw from allocation the market can handle, while keeping macro-control and five-year planning; he does not argue that central planning outperforms markets.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: In "China's Commitment to Peaceful Development" he says colonialism and hegemonism are not viable today, and in the civilizations speech he says no civilization can be judged superior to another.

class-collaboration.rationale: In "Hard Work Makes Dreams Come True" he tells unions to promote harmonious socialist labour relations, and in the 18th Congress study chapter he calls social harmony an inherent attribute of Chinese socialism; the emphasis is on cooperation, not class struggle, in the economy.

collective-farming.rationale: The Third Plenum explanatory notes (All-round and Deeper-level Reform) keep family operation as the fundamental status in agriculture, though he encourages transfer of land-use rights to cooperatives and larger operators.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says all state power belongs to the people and stresses the mass line and people's support ("Commemorate the 30th Anniversary of the Constitution"), but without competitive elections or an opposition, so the evidence is mixed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Across the book (Close Ties with the People, "Strictly Enforce Diligence and Thrift", and "Revolutionize Energy Production and Consumption") he condemns hedonism and extravagance and urges diligence and thrift in consumption.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: In "Exchanges and Mutual Learning Make Civilizations Richer and More Colorful" (UNESCO) he says all civilizations are equal in value and no single civilization can be judged superior.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: In "Accelerate the Development of Housing Security and Supply" he warns against total welfare dependence and wants the market to meet most housing demand, while expanding social security and basic housing elsewhere; evidence points both ways.

defeat-communism.rationale: He is a Communist and calls on Party members to hold firm communist ideals ("Uphold and Develop Socialism"); he opposes the idea of defeating communism.

delink-world-market.rationale: He argues that economies that open up grow and closed ones decline and promotes integration through free-trade areas, Belt and Road and WTO commitments; nothing in the book supports poor countries cutting economic ties with rich ones.

democracy-best.rationale: He holds that China's "whole-process people's democracy" is the most genuine form, rejects multi-party competition, and says China will not copy Western models; he also uses democracy as a goal word, so low confidence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He rejects defining democracy by competitive elections: the 20th Congress report calls whole-process people's democracy the broadest and most genuine form, and he has ruled out a multi-party system and said institutions cannot be imported.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He names the state as a socialist state under the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class ("Commemorate the 30th Anniversary of the Constitution") and lists it among the Four Cardinal Principles; this is close to but not identical to the post-revolution proletarian dictatorship in the statement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He announces absolute emissions reductions and major clean-energy expansion by 2035.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He urges safeguarding the UN’s authority and central global-governance role.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In "Commemorate the 30th Anniversary of the Constitution" he says the Constitution takes root only if all citizens are equal before the law and human rights are respected, though this concerns legal equality as defined by the Chinese system.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He plans continued large coal power bases and more oil and gas output while upgrading coal plants and pursuing a carbon peak and neutrality ("Revolutionize Energy"; 20th Congress report), so the evidence points both ways.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He commits to developing nuclear power actively, safely and orderly.

filial-duty.rationale: In "Strong Ethical Support for the Realization of the Chinese Dream" he praises people who treat the elderly with filial respect and calls for education in family virtues.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He refuses to renounce force against Taiwan separatism and external interference.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: "Safeguard National Security and Social Stability" calls for cracking down on separatist, infiltration and sabotage activities by domestic or foreign hostile forces; the 20th Congress report speaks of external attempts to contain and blackmail China.

free-trade.rationale: He advocates integration, open cooperation and inclusive economic globalisation.

future-generations.rationale: "Usher in a New Era of Ecological Progress" and the letter "Leave to Our Future Generations Blue Skies, Green Fields and Clean Water" both say environmental protection must serve future generations and leave them a clean environment.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: He supports women’s federations and government women-and-children committees implementing equality policy.

gradual-change.rationale: He urges reform that is proactive and steady, with stability as a precondition and top-level design ("Commemorate the 30th Anniversary of the Constitution"; "Economic Growth Must Be Genuine and Not Inflated"), keeping the core institutions fixed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He wants education to build a correct concept of history, national viewpoint and cultural perspective centred on China ("Enhance China's Cultural Soft Power"), and opposes "historical nihilism".

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: China maintains its own nuclear arsenal, which is estimated at about 600 warheads by 2025 and growing under him, and the 20th Congress report lists nuclear security among its safeguards; his speech on nuclear security stresses peaceful use.

independent-unions.rationale: In "Hard Work Makes Dreams Come True" he says Chinese unions are workers organizations under the leadership of the CPC and bridges between Party and workers, and that Party committees should strengthen their leadership over unions; he rejects union independence from the ruling party.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He says no development model is universal ("Carry on the Enduring Spirit of Mao Zedong Thought"), civilizations should not be copied blindly (UNESCO speech) and that China will never blindly copy Western political systems (2021 speech).

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Under his leadership China has expanded its nuclear arsenal to an estimated 600 warheads, building three new missile silo fields for solid-fuel ICBMs and new silos for DF-5 ICBMs; the Notebook calls it among the largest and most rapid modernisation campaigns of the nine nuclear-armed states.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Third Plenum notes keep rural land under collective or state ownership with farmers holding legally protected contracted use rights that may be transferred; this is close to but not the same as holding land only while using it.

leader-cult.rationale: The same 2018 amendments wrote 'Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era' and the sentence that Party leadership is the defining feature of socialism into the Constitution.

limit-growth.rationale: He says China will never again pursue growth at the cost of the environment and must balance growth and protection ("Usher in a New Era of Ecological Progress"), but economic development stays the central task of the Party, so he rejects limiting growth.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: He explicitly supports private enterprise contributing to socialism under Communist Party leadership.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In "The Invisible Hand and the Visible Hand" (Economic Development) he argues the market should play the decisive role in allocating resources and government should cut direct involvement in micro-level allocation, but he stresses the government is not replaceable and that Party leadership is a feature of the system, so he does not hold that markets simply do better than governments.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: In "Align Our Thinking with the Guidelines of the Third Plenary Session" he cites Marx on the economic base determining the superstructure to justify prioritising economic reform, but he also stresses ideals, values and ideology as drivers.

military-superiority.rationale: He sets a goal of a strong, modernised military by the PLA centenary in 2027 but also says China does not engage in an arms race and keeps a defensive posture (Follow the Trend of the Times).

minority-language-support.rationale: Under him the 2021 policy replaced wording guaranteeing minority-language instruction with emphasis on the national language and the 20th Congress report promotes standard spoken and written Chinese; evidence is of policy, not statements.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He lists regional ethnic autonomy among the basic systems to uphold (Commemorate the 30th Anniversary of the Constitution), though under unified state leadership and with a stress on ethnic unity.

multipolar-world.rationale: He explicitly calls for a multipolar world and more democratic international relations.

national-rebirth.rationale: His central theme is the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation after a century of humiliation ("Achieving Rejuvenation Is the Dream of the Chinese People"), though he frames it as steady modernisation rather than radical rebirth from decadence.

national-self-determination.rationale: He backs each people's right to choose its own development path ("Follow the Trend of the Times"), but opposes self-determination for Taiwan, Hong Kong and ethnic regions.

nature-as-capital.rationale: "Usher in a New Era of Ecological Progress" wants economic evaluation norms to count resource consumption, environmental damage and ecological benefits, and the 20th Congress report treats lucid waters and lush mountains as invaluable assets.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He calls for equal access to production factors and fair competition.

one-party-rule.rationale: He reaffirms the Communist Party’s guiding theory and continuing leadership.

online-anonymity.rationale: Under him regulators introduced a real-name system for online platforms and tighter rules in 2020; "Build China into a Cyberpower" calls for supervision of cyberspace in accordance with law.

party-commands-army.rationale: The report insists on absolute party leadership over the armed forces.

party-controls-media.rationale: He requires party leadership of ideological work and stronger online communications management.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He requires all members to adhere to the party’s line and rigorous discipline.

party-own-road.rationale: "Carry on the Enduring Spirit of Mao Zedong Thought" defends independence: Chinese affairs are decided by the Chinese people, there is no universal development model, and no other party or country may dictate.

patriotic-education.rationale: "Enhance China's Cultural Soft Power" calls for education in patriotism, collectivism and socialism through classrooms, history and media so people take more pride in being Chinese; a 2023 Patriotic Education Law followed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: In "The Mass Line" he says many Party officials are losing touch with the people and speaks of formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, and "Power Must Be Caged by the System" admits serious corruption among officials; he says the Party is nonetheless basically sound.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He calls for transmitting traditional Chinese virtues and good family customs.

priority-to-poor.rationale: In "Eliminate Poverty and Accelerate Development in Impoverished Areas" he calls poverty eradication an essential requirement of socialism, tells officials to give poorer areas priority in policy, and in "Economic Growth Must Be Genuine and Not Inflated" asks for a focus on low-income groups; the 20th Congress report claims the end of absolute poverty.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He supports implementing childbirth-support policies to address population ageing.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Third Plenum explanatory notes (All-round and Deeper-level Reform) state that property rights of both the public and non-public sectors are inviolable; the 20th Congress report promises to protect private enterprises property rights by law. He frames this inside socialist public ownership, so it is not an absolute right.

public-ownership.rationale: The Third Plenum explanatory notes (All-round and Deeper-level Reform) insist public ownership keeps the leading role, state capital keeps controlling stakes in natural-monopoly industries, and state capital is directed to key sectors vital to national security and the economy; he pairs this with opening competitive segments and mixed ownership.

region-keeps-system.rationale: He endorses One Country, Two Systems and a high degree of regional autonomy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Third Plenum explanatory notes call for stronger market oversight and fair competition rules; the 20th Congress report promises stronger action against monopolies and law-based regulation of capital, and his government carried out regulatory crackdowns on technology, tutoring and property firms from 2020-21.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He advocates governance reform to narrow the North–South gap.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He treats practice as the criterion of truth and urges solving concrete problems.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He calls for developed countries to provide developing countries financial and technological support.

right-to-secede.rationale: He rejects Taiwan independence and insists on national reunification.

separated-powers.rationale: He calls for a division of labour among decision-making, executive and oversight powers within people's congresses and stresses checks on power ("Power Must Be Caged"), but he rejects Western separation-of-powers constitutionalism and upholds unified state power.

single-official-language.rationale: The 20th Congress report promises to intensify efforts to promote standard spoken and written Chinese, and from 2021 schools in minority regions shifted toward national-language instruction; his statements stop short of restricting other languages.

social-market-economy.rationale: His formula of a market with a decisive allocation role, government macro-control, public services, fair competition rules and social security ("The Invisible Hand and the Visible Hand") sits between laissez-faire and full state running of the economy, though with Party leadership and large state firms.

socialized-markets.rationale: He expressly supports privately owned enterprises, rather than restricting markets to social ownership.

spiritual-nature.rationale: "Enhance Publicity and Theoretical Work" says the Party must promote material, cultural and ethical progress together, and the 20th Congress report says material want is not socialism, nor is cultural impoverishment.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He directs resources toward strategic industries and technological self-reliance.

strong-leader.rationale: He has centralised power (leadership core 2016, Two Establishes, removal of term limits) and the 20th Congress report praises the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee, but he frames this as Party leadership rather than a leader bypassing gridlock.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: His 2022 report to the 20th Party Congress said the Party would remain committed to the principle that religions in China must be Chinese in orientation and provide active guidance so that they adapt to socialist society.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His record includes the 2015 crackdown on human rights lawyers and the 2020 Hong Kong national security law that effectively suppressed the opposition camp; the 20th Congress report cites cracking down on hostile forces and subversion.

surveillance-ok.rationale: "Safeguard National Security and Social Stability" calls for an impregnable anti-terrorism network and for terrorists to be hunted down, and his government built mass surveillance including in Xinjiang under the Strike Hard campaign.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He says China firmly opposes protectionism in any form ("Open Wider to the Outside World") and in the Open World Economy speech; Chinese practice includes tariffs and industrial policy, so medium only.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 20th Congress report says taxation, social security and transfers should regulate income distribution, the personal income tax system be improved and excessive income be adjusted; it gives no tax-rate commitment.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He combines technological modernisation with creative development of traditional Chinese culture.

term-limits.rationale: The 2018 constitutional amendment passed by the National People's Congress under his leadership removed term limits for the President and Vice-President.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He says China opposes hegemonism and will never seek expansion (Commitment to Peaceful Development), while his government expanded its military presence in the South China Sea and promotes Belt and Road influence; evidence is mixed.

traditional-family.rationale: He links harmonious families and proper upbringing to healthy social development.

unions-good.rationale: In "Hard Work Makes Dreams Come True" he calls unions homes for workers, an important pillar supporting the government and tells them to uphold workers legitimate rights including migrant workers and promote harmonious labour relations; he places unions firmly under Party leadership.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He calls for comprehensive universal medical insurance and a strengthened public-health system.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: On 11 March 2018 the National People's Congress, led by his Party, passed by an overwhelming vote (two against, three abstentions) the constitutional amendment removing the two-term limit for the President and Vice-President, announced by Xinhua on 25 February, clearing the way for him to stay in office after 2023.

worker-ownership.rationale: He endorses private businesses and equal treatment of different ownership forms.

notes:
Born 1953. Born 1953. Living-person standard: no inferred answers. The 2025 private-enterprise and population positions take precedence over assumptions from earlier Chinese policy. Democracy rhetoric does not establish acceptance of losing competitive elections; territorial reunification does not establish general territorial expansion.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 67 answers taken from it, 20 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Book answers date from 2012-2014; later positions on Taiwan, democracy, religion, language, birth policy and climate come from the 2022 Congress report and reference sources, and the more recent clear position was used. Where his words (rule of law, people's democracy, opposition to hegemony) differ from his record (term limits removed, Hong Kong and Xinjiang policies, South China Sea), the record decided the answer. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by evidence; five answers that rested only on Wikipedia are re-sourced to the 2018 constitutional amendment as reported by the Made in China Journal (unlimited-reelection, term-limits, leader-cult) and to his 2022 report (subordinate-church-to-state), and keep-nuclear-weapons to the Nuclear Notebook's record of the arsenal expansion under him.
